A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSV research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite the title change and appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original TSV evaluations on four QA benchmarks, including AUROC results in Table 1 and component, sensitivity, and generalization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds pseudo-label noise and class-distribution mismatch experiments in Appendix E.5–E.6, Tables 11–12.

M1.justification: TSV steering, the prototype-based objective, optimal-transport pseudo-labeling, confident sample selection, and inference scoring are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move from Appendix F to Appendix A without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same short-form QA tasks using TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, SciQ, and NQ Open. The new checks perturb labels and exemplar sampling within retained coverage. Vision-language models and long-form QA appear only in discussion or future work.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main, larger-model, GPT-4o, legacy-model, and runtime comparisons. LoRA and LoReFT also remain in Table 4. The new tables compare TSV under different training conditions rather than introduce competing methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 adds controlled pseudo-label flipping, while E.6 constructs exemplar sets with aligned, uniform, or reversed class proportions. These are additional experimental protocols. Section 5.1 also changes the specified BLEURT threshold of 0.5 to a predefined threshold with 0.5 as an example; no alternative value or rerun is documented.

E4.justification: Two targeted robustness analyses are added for LLaMA-3.1-8b: pseudo-label noise on TruthfulQA and exemplar-distribution mismatch on TruthfulQA and SciQ. They extend the existing sample-selection and class-prior analyses by directly manipulating label errors and exemplar composition.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports TSV means and standard deviations across three random seeds. New Tables 11–12 provide point estimates, following the existing appendix practice, without introducing additional run-count information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged. New Table 11 reports AUROCs of 84.2, 83.8, 82.6, 82.2, and 81.3 as pseudo-label noise increases from 5% to 25%. Table 12 adds aligned/uniform/reversed results of 84.2/82.8/82.1 on TruthfulQA and 85.8/82.5/82.7 on SciQ. These are additional condition-specific results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, the MCAR assumption, the probability model, and Equations 1–14 are retained. The new mismatch experiments do not revise the formal assumptions or add mathematical derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight steering for label-efficient hallucination detection, strong benchmark performance, and cross-dataset generalization. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix I explicitly identifies sentence-level detection and short-form QA as applicability boundaries, proposing entity-span localization and long-form decomposition as future directions. Appendix E.5–E.6 adds interpretations of robustness to noisy pseudo-labels and class mismatch, while acknowledging benefits from distribution alignment.

D1.justification: The Impact Statement replaces a promise to release code with a specific repository address and a statement that code is available. Existing implementation details, hardware, and training times are retained. The newly stated main-text Sinkhorn value of 0.05 was already disclosed in v1 Appendix A.1.

R1.justification: New Appendix D substantially expands related-work coverage into object hallucination in large vision-language models, discussing external-model, fine-tuning, and latent-intervention approaches, including Nullu and VTI. Section 2 also replaces the general steering citation to Zou et al. with Im and Li, while additional citations support implementation choices and future directions.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, wording and publication metadata receive localized edits, and Algorithms moves from Appendix F to Appendix A. New related-work and limitations sections expand the appendix structure, but the main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–12 and relocates existing algorithm blocks, with corresponding appendix reflow. Existing figure designs and table structures are preserved; the first page also gains conference publication information.

improvement.justification: The new robustness tests directly examine sensitivity to pseudo-label errors and exemplar imbalance, while Appendix I makes the method's applicability limits clearer. Concrete code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These bounded gains outweigh the less precise BLEURT threshold wording; the core method and main empirical evidence remain unchanged.
